issues.display_title: Issue #3248: [Profile] Integrate Total Block Profile User Like Corrections API
issues.main_description_html:
API issue: GoThruMedia/panorra-api-go#484

Goal

Wire the profile-correction endpoint into the profile page so followers, following, and likes shown in the sidebar exclude interactions coming from blocked, deactivated, and banned users. Today none of the three are corrected, and likes has no value at all.

Endpoint Contract

GET {baseURLGo}/users/total-block-profile/:username

Headers follow the same convention as users/profile/:username:

Header Value
authorization sessionStore.token()
stage mainService.stageEnv()
role sessionStore.role() ?? 'viewer'
ec 'true'

Response is an encrypted envelope (cry + ls, plus e4 when role === 'viewer') and must go through runDecryption() like every other ec: 'true' call. Decrypted payload:

{
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "Total block User",
    "follower": 0,          // excluded by block + deactivate
    "following": 0,
    "likes": 0,
    "follower_banned": 0,   // excluded by ban
    "following_banned": 0,
    "likes_banned": 0
  }
}

Every counter is a subtrahend, not a display value:

displayed followers = max(0, user_count.follower  - follower  - follower_banned)
displayed following = max(0, user_count.following - following - following_banned)
displayed likes     = max(0, user_count.likes     - likes     - likes_banned)

Known API behavior worth designing around:

  • 401 when the role is neither user nor viewer.
  • 409 "User Not Found" — the handler resolves the profile by a real username in the DB. The sentinel my-user that getUserProfile() uses for the own-profile case will 409 here; always pass the route username.
  • For role: viewer only deactivated users are excluded (the block list is per-authenticated-user), so an anonymous visitor gets smaller corrections than a signed-in one. That is expected, not a bug.

Current Frontend State

Location State
repo-wide total-block-profile has zero references — the endpoint is not integrated at all
profile-api.model.ts:1 ProfileApiUserCount declares only follower, following, posts — no likes
profile.model.ts:19 ProfileStats.likes optional, never assigned; comment says "No backing API field yet"
profile.mapper.ts:88 mapProfileApiToUser destructures the raw counters and maps them straight through, no correction
profile-sidebar.component.html:245 renders {{ user().stats.likes ?? '—' }} with a t_profile.t_likes_pending tooltip
profile.component.ts:415 loadUserProfile single getUserProfile() call; own profile is fetched as my-user

So followers / following are currently displayed uncorrected, and likes is a permanent em-dash placeholder.

Blocking Dependency

TotalBlockProfileUser on panorra-api-go@master (src/Api/handlers/Users/UsersHandlers.go:1490) currently returns only follower and following. likes, likes_banned, follower_banned, and following_banned do not exist yet, and API issue #484 is still open.

Separately, user_count is read from the ElasticSearch doc user_<username> with a {follower, following, posts} fallback (UsersHandlers.go:181). It is not confirmed that user_count.likes is emitted at all — and the whole likes formula depends on that base number.

Consequences for this task:

  • The frontend work can land ahead of the backend if every new counter is optional and missing values are treated as 0.
  • The likes stat cannot be verified end-to-end, and the sidebar will keep showing —, until both the base user_count.likes and the correction fields ship.
  • Removing the — placeholder / t_likes_pending tooltip must therefore be the last step, gated on a real response from stage.

Scope of Work

1. profile-api.model.ts

  • Add likes?: number to ProfileApiUserCount.
  • Add ProfileTotalBlockApiData (six optional numeric counters) and ProfileTotalBlockApiEnvelope (data?: ProfileTotalBlockApiData), matching the section-comment style already used in the file.

2. profile.service.ts

  • Add getTotalBlockProfile(username: string) next to getUserProfile, using the header set above.

3. profile.mapper.ts

  • Add an extractTotalBlockCorrections(envelope) helper mirroring extractProfileApiUser, tolerant of a missing/partial payload.
  • Add a pure correctCount(base, excluded, banned) returning Math.max(0, base - excluded - banned).
  • Extend mapProfileApiToUser to take an optional corrections argument and apply it to followers, followersCount, following, and likes. followers still goes through formatProfileCount(); followersCount stays raw for the followers dialog.

4. profile.component.ts

  • Fetch corrections alongside the profile, keyed on the route username (not my-user).
  • The correction call must never block or fail the profile render: on error / timeout, map with zero corrections and log at debug level only.
  • Re-apply corrections when the profile reloads on username change (see clearPostsState).

5. Sidebar + i18n (final step, gated on backend)

  • Drop the ?? '—' fallback and the t_profile.t_likes_pending tooltip once likes resolves to a real number.
  • t_likes_pending exists in all 15 locale files under src/assets/i18n and must be removed from each of them in the same change.

Edge Cases

  • Correction larger than the base count → clamp at 0, never render a negative.
  • user_count.likes absent → keep stats.likes undefined so the placeholder stays; do not coerce to 0, which would falsely read as "no likes".
  • Profile 404 / blocked_by → skip the correction call entirely.
  • Anonymous (viewer) session → still call it; deactivated-user exclusions apply.
  • Own profile → correction call uses the real username while the profile call keeps using my-user.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Sidebar followers / following reflect base counts minus blocked, deactivated, and banned users.
  • Sidebar likes shows a corrected number once the backend emits user_count.likes; until then the existing placeholder remains.
  • No counter can render negative.
  • A failing or slow correction request leaves the profile fully rendered with uncorrected counts — no spinner lock, no error toast.
  • Own-profile view produces the same corrections as another user viewing that profile with no blocks in play.
  • t_likes_pending is removed from all 15 locale files when the placeholder is retired (not before).
  • Unit tests cover correctCount clamping, partial/missing correction payloads, and the mapper wiring.

Out of Scope

  • Backend changes — tracked in panorra-api-go#484.
  • Correcting counts anywhere other than the profile sidebar (post detail, fullscreen, collection composer also read user_count).
  • Any change to the likes tab content, which is served by the self-only users/me/liked endpoint.

Verification

  • Unit tests for the new mapper helpers.
  • Manual check on stage against a profile with a known blocked/deactivated follower: confirm the displayed count drops by exactly the returned correction.
  • Manual check as an anonymous visitor and as the profile owner.
  • Confirm the raw decrypted payload on stage to settle whether user_count.likes is actually emitted.

Product Specification: Web Explore Page

1. Product Overview

The Web Explore Page is the desktop discovery experience for Panora. It adapts the mobile Explore flow into a wider, map-led interface that supports browsing, searching, filtering, previewing, and opening 360° content without forcing users to leave the page.

The page combines:

  • A persistent global sidebar.
  • A unified search and tab system.
  • A filter and sorting toolbar.
  • A synchronized results list and interactive map.
  • Quick 360° previews.
  • A place detail drawer.
  • Empty, loading, and error states.

The design should make discovery faster while preserving feature parity with the mobile Explore experience.

2. Product Objectives

The Web Explore Page should:

  • Make For You the default discovery experience.
  • Support clear switching between Places, 360° Posts, People, and Hashtags.
  • Present search results in both list and map formats.
  • Keep the map and result list synchronized.
  • Let users preview 360° content without losing context.
  • Provide detailed place information in an expandable drawer.
  • Improve information hierarchy, spacing, and action consistency.
  • Support desktop and tablet web layouts.
  • Maintain accessible keyboard and screen-reader behavior.

3. Primary Users

Primary User

A signed-in or guest user who wants to discover nearby places, 360° posts, creators, or hashtags.

User Conditions

Users may:

  • Allow or deny location access.
  • Search manually without location permission.
  • Browse personalized or generic recommendations.
  • Open posts, places, people, or hashtag results.
  • Interact with content based on authentication state.

4. Entry Points

Wireframe

Users can access Explore through:

  • The Explore item in the left sidebar.
  • A shared Explore URL.
  • A location or place link from another page.
  • A search result that opens in Explore context.

5. Default Experience

When Explore loads:

  1. The For You tab is active.
  2. Nearby and personalized recommendations are displayed.
  3. The map centers on the user's location when permission is available.
  4. The list and map show the same result set.
  5. Filters default to Nearby and recommended sorting.
  6. The selected result, if any, is highlighted in both the list and map.

When location permission is unavailable:

  • Use the user's last known region when available.
  • Otherwise use a default market or manually selected location.
  • Display a clear option to enable location or search another area.

6. Information Architecture

6.1 Global Sidebar

The left sidebar should remain visible on desktop and include:

  • Brand logo.
  • Home.
  • Explore.
  • Create.
  • Activity.
  • Messages.
  • Profile.
  • More.

Requirements

  • Explore must show an active state.
  • Each item must include an icon and label.
  • The sidebar may collapse to icon-only mode on narrower screens.
  • Tooltips must appear for icon-only navigation.
  • Notification badges must remain visible and readable.
  • The Create action should remain visually prominent.

6.2 Top Header

The top header includes:

  • Global search field.
  • Keyboard shortcut hint where supported.
  • Current location selector.
  • Theme or display preference control.
  • Account avatar or menu.

Requirements

  • The header remains visible while browsing long result lists.
  • Search must support Places, 360° Posts, People, and Hashtags.
  • The location control should open a location picker.
  • The account menu should not obscure core Explore controls.

6.3 Primary Explore Tabs

The page must include:

  • For You.
  • Places.
  • 360° Posts.
  • People.
  • Hashtags.

Requirements

  • For You is selected by default.
  • The active tab must use more than color alone.
  • Switching tabs updates result type, filters, and map behavior.
  • Tab state should be reflected in the URL.
  • Browser back and forward navigation must restore tab state.
  • Result counts should update after tab changes where applicable.

6.4 Filter and Sorting Toolbar

The toolbar may include:

  • Nearby.
  • Trending.
  • New.
  • Indoor.
  • Outdoor.
  • Business.
  • Most Viewed.
  • Distance.
  • Latest.
  • Recommended.
  • Additional filters.

Requirements

  • Active filters must remain visible.
  • Users must be able to remove filters individually.
  • A Clear all action must appear when multiple filters are active.
  • The toolbar should remain usable with horizontal overflow on smaller layouts.
  • The filter panel must support keyboard navigation.
  • Sorting and filtering must update both the list and the map.

7. Core Layout

7.1 Desktop Split View

The default desktop layout uses:

  • A persistent global sidebar.
  • A result list panel.
  • A map panel.
  • Optional overlay cards and detail drawers.

Recommended Width Allocation

Region Recommended Width
Global sidebar 72 to 88 px
Results panel 380 to 460 px
Map panel Remaining width
Detail drawer 360 to 440 px

Requirements

  • The result list remains independently scrollable.
  • The map remains fixed within the viewport.
  • The list and map must not scroll as one page.
  • The split view must adapt without overlapping controls.
  • A minimum map width must be maintained.

7.2 Tablet Layout

At tablet widths:

  • The sidebar may collapse.
  • The result list may become narrower.
  • The detail drawer may overlay the map.
  • The user may toggle between list and map when space is limited.

7.3 Small-Screen Web Layout

At small web widths:

  • Use a mobile-style Explore layout.
  • Show one primary view at a time.
  • Preserve tabs, filters, quick preview, and detail flows.
  • Keep bottom or compact navigation accessible.

8. Functional Requirements

8.1 Search

The search field should support:

  • Place names.
  • 360° post titles.
  • Usernames and display names.
  • Hashtags.
  • Categories.
  • Locations.

Search Behavior

  • Show recent searches.
  • Show suggested queries.
  • Show matching categories.
  • Support keyboard selection.
  • Debounce requests while typing.
  • Highlight the matched text where practical.
  • Allow users to clear the query.
  • Keep query state in the URL.

Search States

  • Default.
  • Focused.
  • Typing.
  • Loading.
  • Suggestions available.
  • No suggestions.
  • Error.

8.2 Search Results

Each result card should display relevant fields based on result type.

Place Result Card

  • Cover image or 360° thumbnail.
  • Place name.
  • Location.
  • Distance.
  • Category.
  • Short description.
  • View count.
  • Like count.
  • Comment count.
  • Save action.
  • 360° badge when available.

360° Post Result Card

  • 360° thumbnail.
  • Post title.
  • Creator.
  • Location.
  • View count.
  • Like count.
  • Comment count.
  • Save action.
  • Posted date where relevant.

People Result Card

  • Avatar.
  • Display name.
  • Username.
  • Short bio.
  • Follow action.
  • Relevant location or mutual context.

Hashtag Result Card

  • Hashtag.
  • Post count.
  • Representative thumbnails.
  • Follow action where supported.

8.3 Result Selection

When a user selects a result:

  • Highlight the selected card.
  • Highlight the corresponding map marker.
  • Center or pan the map to the selected marker.
  • Open the quick preview card.
  • Preserve the current scroll position.
  • Update the URL without a full page reload.

8.4 Map

The map should support:

  • Pan.
  • Zoom.
  • Recenter to current location.
  • Search this area.
  • Marker clustering.
  • Individual image markers.
  • Selected marker state.
  • Optional map layer control.

Map Requirements

  • Markers must match the current result set.
  • Clusters must display the number of grouped results.
  • Selecting a cluster should zoom or expand grouped results.
  • Hovering a marker may highlight the related card.
  • Selecting a card must highlight the related marker.
  • Map movements should not automatically refresh results until the user selects Search this area, unless live refresh is enabled.
  • The current location marker must be visually distinct.
  • Map controls must not conflict with preview or drawer overlays.

8.5 Quick Preview Card

The quick preview appears over the map after result selection.

Content

  • Thumbnail.
  • Title.
  • Location.
  • Distance.
  • Creator or place owner.
  • View count.
  • Like count.
  • Close action.
  • View 360° action.
  • View details action.

Requirements

  • Only one preview card may be open at a time.
  • It must not hide critical map controls.
  • Closing the card should preserve the selected result unless the user deselects it.
  • The card must be keyboard accessible.
  • Actions must use consistent labels and positions.

8.6 360° Preview Modal

The 360° preview modal allows users to inspect immersive content without leaving Explore.

Features

  • Interactive 360° viewer.
  • Drag and keyboard navigation.
  • Zoom where supported.
  • Thumbnail strip.
  • Fullscreen action.
  • Close action.
  • Content title.
  • Place or creator context.
  • View details action.

Requirements

  • The page behind the modal should remain in its previous state.
  • Focus must remain trapped inside the modal.
  • Closing the modal must return focus to the triggering element.
  • Loading progress must be displayed.
  • A fallback image should appear if immersive rendering fails.
  • The viewer should pause nonessential rendering when the tab is inactive.

8.7 Place Detail Drawer

The place detail drawer opens from the quick preview or result card.

Content

  • Cover image.
  • Place name.
  • Verification state where applicable.
  • Location.
  • Distance.
  • Category.
  • Description.
  • Opening status and hours.
  • Creator or owner.
  • View, like, comment, and save counts.
  • Follow action.
  • Call action where available.
  • Website action where available.
  • Share action.
  • Related 360° posts.
  • Nearby places.

Requirements

  • The drawer should open from the map side or right edge.
  • The drawer must be independently scrollable.
  • The map should remain visible where screen width allows.
  • The selected marker must remain highlighted.
  • Closing the drawer should return to the quick preview or base Explore state.
  • Drawer state should be represented in the URL where practical.

8.8 Interactions

Supported interactions include:

  • Like.
  • Comment.
  • Save.
  • Share.
  • Follow.
  • Open profile.
  • Open place details.
  • View 360°.
  • Open external website.
  • Call a place.

Authentication Behavior

For restricted actions:

  • Signed-in users should complete the action directly.
  • Guest users should receive a sign-in prompt.
  • The interface should preserve the intended action after authentication where possible.

9. Content Synchronization

The result list, map, preview card, modal, and detail drawer must share one synchronized selection state.

Synchronization Rules

  • Selecting a list card highlights the map marker.
  • Selecting a marker highlights and scrolls to the list card.
  • Opening a preview does not change active filters.
  • Opening a drawer does not clear the selected marker.
  • Changing filters updates all visible result surfaces.
  • Closing a modal restores the previous drawer or preview state.
  • Browser navigation restores the relevant tab, filters, query, selected result, and open panel state.

10. States and Feedback

10.1 Loading State

Display:

  • Skeleton result cards.
  • Map loading placeholder.
  • Disabled actions until data is ready.
  • Progressive loading for images and 360° content.

10.2 Empty State

Display when no results match the query or filters.

Required Content

  • Clear empty-state illustration or icon.
  • Message: No places or 360° posts found.
  • Guidance to adjust filters or search another area.
  • Clear all filters action.
  • Search this area on map action.

10.3 Error State

Use specific messages for:

  • Search failure.
  • Map failure.
  • Location permission failure.
  • Content loading failure.
  • 360° rendering failure.
  • Save, like, or follow action failure.

The system should preserve the user's current filters and query after recoverable errors.

10.4 Offline State

When offline:

  • Show cached content when available.
  • Disable actions that require the server.
  • Explain that results may be outdated.
  • Offer retry after reconnection.

11. URL and State Management

The page should encode important state in the URL.

Recommended Parameters

  • Active tab.
  • Search query.
  • Filters.
  • Sort order.
  • Map center.
  • Zoom level.
  • Selected result.
  • Open detail drawer.
  • Open 360° preview.

Requirements

  • Shared links should reopen the same Explore context where possible.
  • Invalid or expired selections should fall back gracefully.
  • Sensitive data must not be placed in the URL.

12. Accessibility Requirements

The page should conform to WCAG 2.1 AA.

Requirements

  • All controls must support keyboard operation.
  • Focus order must follow visual order.
  • Tabs must use appropriate ARIA roles.
  • Map markers must have accessible alternatives.
  • Result cards must expose meaningful names and states.
  • Active filters must be announced.
  • Modal focus must be trapped.
  • Drawer state changes must be announced.
  • Color must not be the only indicator of selection.
  • Text and controls must meet contrast requirements.
  • Tap and click targets should be at least 44 × 44 CSS pixels where practical.
  • Motion should respect reduced-motion preferences.
  • 360° content must include a non-immersive fallback.

13. Responsive Requirements

Breakpoint Behavior
1440 px and above Full sidebar, list, map, preview, and non-overlapping detail drawer
1024 to 1439 px Compact sidebar, narrower list, overlay drawer
768 to 1023 px Collapsed sidebar, list-map toggle, overlay details
Below 768 px Mobile-style Explore flow

The exact breakpoints may follow the product design system.

14. Performance Requirements

Metric Target
Initial meaningful render Under 2.5 seconds on a typical broadband connection
Search suggestion response Under 500 milliseconds
Filter update Under 1 second
Map interaction response Under 100 milliseconds
Preview card open Under 300 milliseconds after data is available
Detail drawer open Under 500 milliseconds
360° viewer first frame Under 3 seconds on a supported connection
Layout shift score Below 0.1
Crash-free sessions At least 99.8%

Performance Practices

  • Lazy-load images outside the viewport.
  • Use responsive image sizes.
  • Virtualize long result lists.
  • Cluster markers at lower zoom levels.
  • Defer immersive viewer assets until requested.
  • Cache common filters and recent searches.
  • Avoid reloading the full map after minor UI changes.

15. Privacy and Safety Requirements

  • Request location permission only when needed.
  • Explain the benefit before requesting location.
  • Do not expose exact private user locations.
  • Sanitize search queries and user-generated text.
  • Validate outbound URLs.
  • Apply platform moderation to thumbnails and immersive content.
  • Prevent unauthorized access to private posts or restricted places.
  • Do not include sensitive content in analytics payloads.
  • Comply with account blocking and content visibility rules.

16. Analytics Events

Event Trigger
explore_opened User opens Explore
explore_tab_changed User changes the primary tab
explore_search_started User focuses or begins typing in search
explore_search_submitted User submits a query
explore_filter_applied User applies a filter
explore_filter_removed User removes a filter
explore_sort_changed User changes sorting
explore_result_selected User selects a result
explore_marker_selected User selects a map marker
explore_cluster_selected User selects a map cluster
explore_search_area_clicked User searches within the current map area
explore_preview_opened Quick preview opens
explore_360_opened 360° preview opens
explore_detail_opened Detail drawer opens
explore_like_clicked User likes content
explore_save_clicked User saves content
explore_follow_clicked User follows a creator or place
explore_share_clicked User opens sharing
explore_empty_state_shown No results are available
explore_error_shown A recoverable Explore error appears

Analytics must not capture raw private location data or full search text when policy prohibits it.

17. Acceptance Criteria

AC-01: Default For You Experience

Given the user opens Explore
When the page finishes loading
Then the For You tab is active
And recommended content appears in the result list and map.

AC-02: Unified Tab Navigation

Given the user is on Explore
When the user selects Places, 360° Posts, People, or Hashtags
Then the result type changes
And the active tab is clearly indicated
And the URL reflects the selected tab.

AC-03: Search Suggestions

Given the user focuses the search field
When the user enters a query
Then the system displays recent or suggested searches
And supports keyboard selection
And allows the query to be cleared.

AC-04: Search Submission

Given the user enters a valid query
When the user submits the search
Then matching results appear
And the map updates when the result type supports location.

AC-05: Filters and Sorting

Given the user applies one or more filters
When the system updates the results
Then the list and map display the same filtered result set
And active filters remain visible
And the user can clear them.

AC-06: Result and Marker Synchronization

Given a result is visible in the list and map
When the user selects the list card
Then the related marker is highlighted
And the map centers on the result when needed.

Given the user selects a marker
Then the related result card is highlighted
And scrolled into view.

AC-07: Search This Area

Given the user moves the map
When the visible area changes
Then a Search this area control appears.

When the user selects it
Then results refresh for the current map bounds.

AC-08: Quick Preview

Given the user selects a supported result
Then a quick preview appears over the map
And displays View 360° and View details actions.

AC-09: Open 360° Preview

Given a selected result includes 360° content
When the user selects View 360°
Then the immersive preview opens
And the prior Explore state remains preserved.

AC-10: Close 360° Preview

Given the 360° preview is open
When the user closes it
Then focus returns to the triggering control
And the previous selection remains active.

AC-11: Place Detail Drawer

Given a place result is selected
When the user selects View details
Then the detail drawer opens
And shows place information, actions, related posts, and nearby places.

AC-12: Empty State

Given no results match the query or filters
Then the system displays the empty state
And provides Clear all filters and Search this area actions.

AC-13: Authentication-Gated Action

Given a guest user selects Like, Save, Follow, or Comment
Then the system displays a sign-in prompt
And preserves the intended action where possible.

AC-14: Browser Navigation

Given the user changes tabs, filters, or selected content
When the user uses browser back or forward
Then the relevant Explore state is restored without a full application reset.

AC-15: Responsive Layout

Given the browser width changes
Then the layout adapts according to the supported breakpoint
And no critical control becomes inaccessible.

AC-16: Keyboard Accessibility

Given a keyboard-only user opens Explore
Then the user can access tabs, filters, result cards, map alternatives, preview controls, modal controls, and drawer actions.

AC-17: Recoverable Error

Given a search or map request fails
Then the system shows a clear error
And retains the user's query, filters, and selection
And provides a retry action.

18. Non-Goals

The first release does not need to include:

  • Full route planning or turn-by-turn navigation.
  • Advanced map drawing tools.
  • Offline 360° downloads.
  • Multi-user collaborative collections.
  • User-generated map layers.
  • Real-time live location sharing.

19. Definition of Done

The Web Explore Page is complete when:

  • The desktop layout matches the approved wireframe.
  • For You, Places, 360° Posts, People, and Hashtags are functional.
  • Search, filters, and sorting update the correct result set.
  • The result list and map remain synchronized.
  • Quick preview, 360° modal, and detail drawer work as specified.
  • Empty, loading, offline, and error states are implemented.
  • URL state and browser navigation are verified.
  • Responsive behavior is tested across supported breakpoints.
  • Accessibility testing passes.
  • Performance targets are validated.
  • Analytics events are confirmed.
  • Security, privacy, and moderation reviews are complete.
  • Automated and manual acceptance tests pass.

🔌 Integrate — Contact Us

task BE:

  • GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new#414

Demo by Developer

contact-us.webm

🧑‍💻 Frontend update — 14 August 2026

Branch: new-flow-content-us

The Contact Us form is wired to POST /contact-us and POST /attachment. After the backend task (panorra-api-new#414) shipped through panorra-api-new#415 (merged into development on 30 July 2026, commit 6f73686), I audited our payload against the merged API source — not the issue description — and found five mismatches. All five are fixed.

Contract mismatches found and fixed

# Problem Impact before fix Fix
1 We sent full_name; the API reads fullname Guest (viewer-role) submissions rejected with 400 Required Fullname contact-us-form.component.ts — field renamed
2 Dropdown offered 7 subject codes; the API enum has 4 feedback, bug, partnership → 422 Invalid Subject, submission fails completely contact-us.data.ts now mirrors normalizeContactSubject (feature, performance, software, other); labels trimmed in all 15 i18n bundles
3 Client accepted image/webp and image/gif File passes client validation, then rejected by the API with 400 ACCEPTED_ATTACHMENT_TYPES now mirrors the API allowlist (jpg/jpeg, png, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, txt)
4 attachments payload carried only u_name Support inbox shows the generated storage name (20260814….a1b2c3.pdf) instead of the user's filename uploadedNames() now sends { u_name, original_filename }, which is what contactAttachmentDisplayName labels the email link with
5 No per-file size check on the client 2 MB cap only surfaced after a full upload round-trip ATTACHMENT_MAX_FILE_SIZE + isAcceptedSize(); oversized files never enter the upload queue

Accepted attachment types (POST /attachment)

Single source of truth on the client: ACCEPTED_ATTACHMENT_TYPES in src/app/pages/contact-us/contact-us-attachment.service.ts. It also feeds the file input's accept attribute, so the OS file picker and our validation cannot drift apart.

Extension MIME type sent by the browser Accepted
.png image/png ✅
.jpg / .jpeg image/jpeg ✅
.pdf application/pdf ✅
.doc application/msword ✅
.docx application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document ✅
.xls application/vnd.ms-excel ✅
.xlsx application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet ✅
.txt text/plain ✅
.webp image/webp ❌ not in the API allowlist
.gif image/gif ❌ not in the API allowlist
anything else — ❌

Limits enforced on both sides: max 5 attachments per submission and 2 MB per file.

Two behaviours worth knowing for QA:

  • The client and the API validate differently. We check File.type, which the browser derives from the extension. The API sniffs the actual file content (http.DetectContentType) and only falls back to the extension when the sniff returns application/zip or application/octet-stream — the two cases Go's sniffer cannot resolve for Office formats. A file renamed to a permitted extension therefore passes our check and is still rejected by the API with 400 Attachment type not valid. That is the intended layering, not a bug.
  • .jpg and .jpeg are the same entry. Browsers report image/jpeg for both; there is no image/jpg MIME type, so the list needs one entry, not two.

Uploads run sequentially, one request per file, and each file's status (pending / uploading / uploaded / error) is rendered per row with a retry action on failure. Only files in uploaded state are included in the attachments payload at submit time, and submitting is blocked while any upload is still pending or failed.

Related changes in the same area

  • The attachment list now shows the picked file name instead of u_name — the latter is replaced by the server-generated storage name once the upload succeeds, so the user saw a hash where their filename used to be.
  • The dropzone is hidden once the 5-file limit is reached.
  • POST /attachment responses are now typed (AttachmentUploadResponse), including thumbnail: string | null — the API returns null for non-image attachments where it previously always returned a string.
  • The five toasts in ContactUsAttachmentService were hardcoded English. They now go through t_contact_us.attachments.toast* and are translated in all 15 locales, matching how the rest of this page handles toasts.

Verification

  • ng test --include="src/app/pages/contact-us/**" → 30/30 pass. Baseline before this work was 26 tests with 12 failing: two specs never provided TranslateModule.forRoot() while their components inject TranslateService. Fixed as part of this change.
  • New test coverage: webp/gif rejection, oversized-file rejection (not queued for upload), original_filename in the submit payload including its fallback path, and the filename shown in the list.
  • ng build --configuration development → exit 0. The three NG8113 warnings come from home/detail-place and home/place, unrelated to this work.
  • All 15 i18n bundles re-validated: valid JSON, 4 subjectOptions each, 5 new toast keys each.

Against the acceptance criteria

Criterion Status
Signal-driven loading state, no double submit ✅ submitting signal drives zLoading / zDisabled on the submit button
Validation blocks submit with clear guidance ✅ typed reactive form; markAllAsTouched() on invalid submit
Success + error toasts; typed input preserved on error ✅ form only resets on success
No console errors ✅ none in the test run or dev build
Submits via a facade/service ⚠️ partial — attachments are isolated in ContactUsAttachmentService, but the submit call still lives in ContactUsFormComponent and hits FatchApiService directly. ContactUsFacade is currently content/i18n only. Moving submit behind the facade is still open.
No any ⚠️ not met — api.post<any>, decrypted: any, and catch (error: any) remain. Needs the response envelope typed, which pairs naturally with the facade work above.

Needs a decision

  1. Subject options. Feedback, Bug Report and Partnership are gone from the dropdown because the API rejects them. If product wants all seven, the right fix is extending normalizeContactSubject on the API side — mapping them silently to other would cost support the context. Please confirm which way to go.
  2. Guest submissions. The merged API accepts submissions from viewer-role sessions using fullname / email from the form. Should Contact Us be reachable while logged out in the PWA? This decides whether the form is shown to guests at all.
  3. Rate limiting. /contact-us is capped at 5 requests/minute per IP and the attachment download at 60/minute. There is no dedicated 429 message yet — currently it falls through to the generic error toast.
  4. 2 MB cap on documents. The cap was sized for screenshots and now also applies to PDFs and Office files; a scanned multi-page PDF clears it easily. This was raised in the API review and left unanswered. The dropzone helper text also does not mention the size limit yet.

Items 1 and 2 block final QA sign-off; 3 and 4 are follow-ups.

Update: Integrate Profile Liked Posts API

Status: implemented — branch 3246-profile-integrate-profile-liked-posts-api (commit 18e79ba, 27 files, +421/−17). PR not opened yet.

The Like tab on the profile page is now wired to the real endpoint. It previously hard-coded return [] with a "no endpoint yet" comment in three places (activePosts, isLoadingCurrentTab, canLoadMore) — all three now carry real state.

1. Endpoint contract → what it forces on the frontend

GET {baseURLGo}/users/me/liked?limit={limit}&page={page}
headers: authorization, stage, role, ec: true
resp   : encrypted → runDecryption() → { data: { posts: [{ slug, thumbnail }], total, page, limit } }
order  : l.updated_at DESC (BE)
Endpoint fact Frontend consequence
Takes no :username, resolves the user from the token self-only — another user's likes cannot be listed at all
Rejects anything but role: user with 401 the request must be gated on an authenticated session
Item payload is only slug + thumbnail no dimensions → aspect ratio must fall back
Reports data.total the last page can be detected exactly

Published / private / banned / blocked / deactivated filtering is already handled by the BE, so there is no second round of filtering on the client.

2. Service + models

profile.service.ts — getLikedPosts(page, limit), same header pattern as the other profile endpoints, with a doc comment marking it self-only so callers don't reach for it on someone else's profile.

profile-api.model.ts — ProfileLikedPostApiItem (slug, thumbnail) + ProfileLikedPostsApiEnvelope (posts, total, page, limit).

profile.model.ts — ProfileUser.likes: ProfilePost[], and the ProfileContentTab doc updated from "has no backing endpoint yet" to self-only + privacy notice.

profile.mapper.ts — mapLikedPostApiToProfilePost():

export function mapLikedPostApiToProfilePost(
  item: ProfileLikedPostApiItem,
  renderImageUrl: (url: string) => string,
): ProfilePost {
  return {
    id: item.slug ?? `liked-${Math.random()}`,
    slug: item.slug,
    imageUrl: item.thumbnail ? renderImageUrl(item.thumbnail) : '',
    aspectRatio: DEFAULT_ASPECT_RATIO,
  };
}

The endpoint sends no width/height/panorama_quality, so DEFAULT_ASPECT_RATIO keeps the justified and bento layouts stable (no reflow). mapProfileApiToUser also carries likes: currentUser?.likes ?? [] through so the list isn't dropped when the profile is refetched.

3. Fetch, pagination, reset (profile.component.ts)

New state: loadingLikes, hasMoreLikes, likePage — following the posts/tagged/bookmark pattern.

protected loadUserLikes(): void {
  if (this.loadingLikes()) return;
  if (!this.isOwnProfile() || !this.sessionStore.isLoggedIn()) return;
  ...
}
  • Guard: no username argument; if this isn't your own profile or you aren't logged in, the request never fires — so there is no request that is guaranteed to 401.
  • Dedup by id (slug) before appending, like the other tabs.
  • hasMoreLikes from data.total: 
    this.hasMoreLikes.set(
  typeof total === 'number'
    ? this.user().likes.length < total
    : newLikes.length >= PAGE_LIMIT,
);
    Because this endpoint reports total, the last page is detected exactly instead of costing one extra empty request like the page-size heuristic the other tabs use. The heuristic is kept as a fallback in case total is absent.
  • Error handling: likePage is rolled back (Math.max(1, likePage - 1)) so a retry or the next scroll doesn't skip a page.
  • Reset on profile switch: likePage = 1, hasMoreLikes.set(false) and likes: [] added to the existing reset.
  • Infinite scroll: a tab === 'likes' branch added to triggerLoadMore().

4. The tab stays visible on other profiles → privacy notice

The Like tab is not hidden on someone else's profile. What changes is its content.

profile-gallery.component.ts:

protected readonly isLikesRestricted = computed(() => this.isLikesTab() && !this.isOwnProfile());
  • The lazy-load effect only emits loadLikes when isOwnProfile() is true, and is keyed by username so it doesn't replay when you come back to your own profile.
  • isResolvingCurrentTab() short-circuits for a restricted tab: 
    // Nothing is ever requested for a restricted tab, so the notice is its settled
// state — without this it would sit on skeletons forever.
if (this.isLikesRestricted()) return false;
    This matters: since no request will ever settle, without the short-circuit the tab would show skeletons indefinitely.

profile-gallery-empty.component.ts — dedicated copy:

const RESTRICTED_LIKES_COPY: EmptyStateCopy = {
  title: 't_profile.t_private_likes_title',
  description: 't_profile.t_private_likes_desc',
  icon: 'fa-regular fa-lock',
};

With new isRestricted + username inputs and a descriptionParams computed for the {{username}} interpolation. Rendered result:

🔒 This user's liked panoramas are private
Panoramas liked by alice are currently hidden

All three empty-state usages in the template (uniform / bento / justified) pass [isRestricted] + [username]. fa-regular fa-lock was already in fontawesome-subset.css, so no subset regeneration was needed.

5. Bug found along the way: cross-attribution on the post detail page

Posts in the Like tab belong to other users. openPostDetail() previously passed from=profile plus the currently viewed profile as nav state, so the detail page used that profile's timeline as prev/next and as the source of totalPosts — even though the post isn't theirs.

// `from=profile` makes the detail page treat this profile's timeline as the
// post's siblings (prev/next + post count). A liked post is someone else's, so
// it is opened standalone and the viewer falls back to its default feed context.
if (this.isLikesTab()) {
  void this.router.navigate(['/post', post.slug ?? post.id]);
  return;
}

aria-label and alt were also switched to t_common.t_view_post instead of t_profile.t_post_by / t_view_post_by, which say "post by {username}" — the wrong attribution for someone else's post.

6. i18n

It turned out the entire likes block (t_likes, t_likes_pending, t_empty_likes_title, t_empty_likes_desc) only existed in en.json — the other 14 locales would render raw keys, including the tab label itself. Patched as part of this work:

  • en.json: +2 keys (t_private_likes_title, t_private_likes_desc)
  • the other 14 locales: +6 keys each (the 4 missing likes keys + the 2 privacy-notice keys)

Spliced surgically without reformatting the JSON, and all 15 bundles validated with JSON.parse.

7. Verification

  • ng build --configuration development — clean.
  • Gallery specs — 11/11 SUCCESS, including 5 new tests in describe('ProfileGalleryComponent likes tab'):
    1. the Like tab is offered on every profile;
    2. another user's profile → privacy notice, 0 skeletons;
    3. another user's profile → loadLikes is never emitted;
    4. own profile → exactly 1 request even after switching away and back;
    5. own profile + empty response → the ordinary empty state, not the privacy notice.
  • Lint on src/app/pages/profile/** — 34 errors / 5 warnings, identical to the pre-change baseline (0 new findings).

Notes / follow-up

  • The "Likes" stat in the sidebar still shows —. That is likes received, which comes from a different endpoint and is handled in #3248 — separate from this tab.
  • Once #3248 fills that number in, t_profile.t_likes will be shared by the tab (likes given) and the stat slot (likes received); the copy should be differentiated to avoid ambiguity.

Panorra Offline Handling — Product Specification

Product and engineering specification for the Panorra Next.js PWA offline experience.

1. Document Purpose

This document defines the approved offline-handling scope for Panorra.

The selected solution is intentionally simple:

When Panorra cannot reach the internet, show a dedicated No Internet Connection screen with clear recovery actions.

Panorra will not implement full offline browsing, downloaded place data, offline maps, queued social actions, background synchronization, or automatic 360° media caching in the first version.

The goal is to provide a polished and reliable user experience while avoiding unnecessary engineering cost, operational complexity, storage issues, and data-consistency risks.

2. Product Decision

Approved solution

Panorra will implement:

  • A dedicated offline fallback screen
  • A connection retry action
  • A return-to-home or return-to-explore action
  • Light-mode and dark-mode support
  • The existing Panorra sidebar navigation
  • A Panorra-branded illustration using the logo gradient
  • Optional compact offline and back-online notifications
  • Automatic recovery when the connection becomes available again

Out of scope

Panorra will not initially implement:

  • Full offline feed browsing
  • Offline place-detail storage
  • Offline map tiles
  • Downloaded maps
  • Automatic 360° image caching
  • Automatic 360° video caching
  • Background upload synchronization
  • Offline likes, saves, comments, or community actions
  • IndexedDB data synchronization
  • Conflict resolution
  • Multi-device offline reconciliation
  • Offline analytics event queues
  • Storage-management screens

3. Why This Solution Was Chosen

3.1 It solves the real user problem

The main user problem is not that every Panorra feature must work offline.

The actual problem is:

Users need to understand why content cannot load and what they can do next.

A clear offline screen solves this directly by:

  • Explaining that the connection is unavailable
  • Preventing confusing loading states
  • Providing a retry action
  • Providing a safe navigation option
  • Preserving Panorra’s brand experience

3.2 It avoids disproportionate engineering work

A complete offline-first platform would require substantial work across:

  • Service workers
  • Cache versioning
  • IndexedDB
  • Background synchronization
  • API mutation queues
  • Conflict resolution
  • Storage quotas
  • Media download management
  • Cache invalidation
  • Authentication-state handling
  • Cross-device consistency
  • Offline analytics
  • Quality assurance across browsers

This investment is not justified unless product data proves that users frequently need offline access to saved Panorra content.

3.3 Panorra content is expensive to cache

Panorra handles:

  • 360° photos
  • 360° videos
  • High-resolution thumbnails
  • Maps
  • Location data
  • User-generated content

These assets can consume significant storage and bandwidth.

Automatic caching could create:

  • Excessive disk usage
  • Slow downloads
  • Outdated content
  • Broken media references
  • Poor performance on low-end devices
  • Unexpected mobile-data consumption

3.4 It reduces data-consistency risks

Offline write operations can create complex states.

Examples:

  • A user joins a community offline, but the community becomes private before synchronization.
  • A user likes a deleted post.
  • A user uploads media after authentication expires.
  • A saved place changes or is removed.
  • The same action is submitted more than once.

Supporting these cases correctly requires:

  • Idempotency
  • Retry rules
  • Conflict resolution
  • Error recovery
  • User-visible sync states
  • Server-side support

The no-internet screen avoids these risks.

3.5 It is easier to test and maintain

The approved solution has a small and predictable test surface.

The engineering team only needs to validate:

  • Offline detection
  • Screen rendering
  • Retry behavior
  • Navigation behavior
  • Theme behavior
  • Responsive layout
  • Recovery when the connection returns

This is significantly more maintainable than a full offline architecture.

3.6 It supports future expansion

The simple solution does not prevent future offline features.

Panorra can later add offline capabilities incrementally based on evidence, such as:

  1. Saved drafts
  2. Explicit 360° media downloads
  3. Saved place details
  4. Lightweight queued actions
  5. Offline maps

The current implementation creates a stable foundation without committing to unnecessary complexity.

4. Product Goals

Primary goals

  • Clearly communicate that Panorra cannot reach the internet
  • Prevent indefinite loading states
  • Provide an obvious retry action
  • Provide a safe way to return to Panorra’s main area
  • Maintain a polished Panorra-branded experience
  • Work consistently in light and dark themes
  • Require minimal engineering and maintenance effort

Secondary goals

  • Detect when the connection returns
  • Allow the user to retry without manually refreshing the browser
  • Optionally notify the user when Panorra is back online
  • Keep the existing sidebar visible when appropriate

5. Non-Goals

The first version is not intended to:

  • Make Panorra fully functional offline
  • Persist user-generated activity while offline
  • Cache all previously viewed content
  • Provide downloadable maps
  • Guarantee offline access to media
  • Synchronize queued actions
  • Replace the service worker with a complex offline data layer
  • Support offline-first workflows

6. User Experience Specification

6.1 Main offline screen

WIreframe

The offline screen must contain:

  • Panorra sidebar navigation
  • Panorra logo
  • Branded offline illustration
  • Main heading
  • Supporting message
  • Primary retry button
  • Secondary return button

Recommended copy

Heading

No internet connection

Supporting text

We can’t load this page right now because you’re offline.
Check your connection and try again.

Primary button

Try again

Secondary button

Go back home

Alternative:

Go to Explore

6.2 Illustration

The illustration should:

  • Use Panorra’s pink, violet, and blue gradient
  • Match the visual language of the Panorra logo
  • Communicate connection loss without feeling alarming
  • Remain decorative and not replace explanatory text
  • Work on both light and dark backgrounds

Recommended visual elements:

  • A stylized planet or globe
  • Orbit lines
  • Small stars or clouds
  • A disconnected Wi-Fi symbol
  • Soft blue-violet and pink gradients

6.3 Sidebar

The offline screen should use the existing Panorra sidebar rather than a top navigation header.

The sidebar should preserve:

  • Panorra logo
  • Existing navigation icons
  • Active navigation treatment
  • Notification badge
  • Create button
  • User avatar

Navigation actions that require internet may remain visible, but selecting them while offline must continue to show the offline experience rather than entering a broken loading state.

6.4 Light mode

Recommended colors:

Role Value
Page background #FFFFFF or #F7F8FB
Primary text #1F2937
Secondary text #6B7280
Primary action #6F64E6
Gradient accent #FF7ACB → #A78BFF → #6F64E6
Border #E5E7EB
Card surface #FFFFFF

6.5 Dark mode

Recommended colors:

Role Value
Page background #0B1020
Surface #12182A
Primary text #F8FAFC
Secondary text #CBD5E1
Primary action #6F64E6
Hover accent #8A82F2
Border #283149
Gradient accent #FF7ACB → #A78BFF → #6F64E6

The official primary remains #6F64E6 in both themes.

Lighter variants may be used for hover, focus, and small active indicators in dark mode.

7. Interaction Specification

7.1 Try again

When the user selects Try again:

  1. Panorra checks whether the application backend is reachable.
  2. The button enters a loading state.
  3. If reachable, the page retries the original route.
  4. If still unreachable, the screen remains visible.
  5. The user receives non-blocking feedback.

Recommended loading label:

Checking connection…

Recommended failure feedback:

Still offline. Check your connection and try again.

7.2 Go back home

When the user selects Go back home:

  • Navigate to the Panorra home or Explore route.
  • If that route cannot load, keep the user on the offline fallback.
  • Do not create a redirect loop.

7.3 Automatic recovery

When the browser fires an online event:

  1. Panorra performs a lightweight connectivity check.
  2. If the backend is reachable, retry the original page.
  3. Optionally show a success toast.

Recommended toast:

Back online
You’re connected. Enjoy exploring!

The application must not trust navigator.onLine alone. A backend health check should confirm connectivity.

8. Connection States

Panorra should use the following states:

type ConnectionState =
  | "checking"
  | "online"
  | "offline";

Checking

  • Used during initial verification and retry
  • Shows loading feedback
  • Prevents repeated retry clicks

Online

  • Normal application behavior
  • Offline screen is hidden
  • The requested route may load

Offline

  • Offline fallback is visible
  • Network-dependent content is not requested repeatedly
  • Retry and return actions remain available

9. Recommended Next.js Structure

app/
├── offline/
│   └── page.tsx
├── api/
│   └── health/
│       └── route.ts
└── layout.tsx

src/
├── components/
│   └── connectivity/
│       ├── offline-screen.tsx
│       ├── offline-illustration.tsx
│       ├── connectivity-toast.tsx
│       └── retry-connection-button.tsx
├── hooks/
│   └── use-connectivity.ts
└── providers/
    └── connectivity-provider.tsx

10. Health Check Endpoint

Recommended endpoint:

HEAD /api/health

Expected online response:

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Cache-Control: no-store

Example:

import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

export function HEAD() {
  return new NextResponse(null, {
    status: 204,
    headers: {
      "Cache-Control": "no-store",
    },
  });
}

The endpoint should:

  • Be lightweight
  • Require no authentication
  • Return no user data
  • Avoid database access where possible
  • Disable caching

11. Offline Detection Logic

Recommended behavior:

async function checkConnection():
  Promise<boolean> {
  if (!navigator.onLine) {
    return false;
  }

  try {
    const response = await fetch("/api/health", {
      method: "HEAD",
      cache: "no-store",
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(4000),
    });

    return response.ok;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

This combines:

  • Browser connectivity events
  • A real application-reachability check
  • A short timeout
  • Safe error handling

12. Service Worker Scope

The service worker should remain minimal.

Recommended responsibilities:

  • Cache the offline fallback page
  • Cache essential static assets
  • Cache the Panorra logo
  • Cache the offline illustration
  • Cache required fonts or use system fallbacks
  • Return the offline page for failed navigation requests

The service worker should not initially:

  • Cache dynamic feed data
  • Cache authenticated API responses
  • Cache private messages
  • Cache map tiles
  • Cache full 360° media
  • Queue mutations
  • Manage background synchronization

13. Functional Acceptance Criteria

Offline detection

  • The application detects when the browser loses network access.
  • The application confirms backend reachability before declaring itself online.
  • A failed health check changes the connection state to offline.
  • Detection does not block the main thread.
  • Network-check failures do not crash the application.

Offline screen

  • The offline screen appears when the requested page cannot load.
  • The screen includes the Panorra sidebar.
  • The screen includes the Panorra logo.
  • The screen includes a Panorra-gradient illustration.
  • The heading reads “No internet connection.”
  • The supporting message explains the situation.
  • A primary “Try again” action is visible.
  • A secondary navigation action is visible.
  • The screen is responsive.

Retry behavior

  • Selecting Try again initiates a new health check.
  • The button shows a loading state during the check.
  • Repeated clicks are prevented during checking.
  • A successful check reloads or retries the requested route.
  • A failed check keeps the offline screen visible.
  • The failure message is clear and non-blocking.

Recovery behavior

  • Panorra listens for browser online events.
  • An online event triggers a health check.
  • Successful recovery returns the user to the requested page.
  • An optional back-online toast can be displayed.
  • The application does not enter a reload loop.

Theme behavior

  • The offline screen supports light mode.
  • The offline screen supports dark mode.
  • The official primary color remains #6F64E6.
  • The illustration uses the Panorra logo gradient.
  • Text and controls remain readable in both themes.
  • Visible focus states are provided.

Sidebar behavior

  • The existing sidebar layout is used.
  • Sidebar spacing matches the production application.
  • Navigation icons remain recognizable.
  • The notification badge remains correctly positioned.
  • The user avatar remains visible.
  • Network-dependent sidebar actions do not produce broken pages.

14. Non-Functional Acceptance Criteria

Performance

  • The offline screen loads from the service-worker cache.
  • Essential offline assets remain small.
  • The fallback does not require an API response to render.
  • The health check completes or times out within four seconds.
  • No large media files are precached.

Accessibility

  • The heading uses a semantic heading element.
  • Buttons are keyboard accessible.
  • Focus states are visible.
  • Status feedback uses aria-live.
  • The illustration has appropriate alternative handling.
  • Color is not the only way status is communicated.
  • Touch targets are at least 44 by 44 pixels.
  • The layout remains usable at 200% zoom.

Reliability

  • The fallback works after a production build.
  • The fallback works in the installed PWA.
  • The fallback works after refreshing while offline.
  • The solution works in supported Chromium browsers.
  • Unsupported service-worker environments degrade safely.
  • The offline screen does not expose application errors.

Maintainability

  • Offline logic is centralized.
  • UI components do not independently implement network detection.
  • The health endpoint is documented.
  • Copy and visual tokens are reusable.
  • The service-worker configuration remains minimal.
  • Offline behavior is covered by automated tests where practical.

15. Test Scenarios

Scenario 1: Connection lost on an open page

  1. Open Panorra while online.
  2. Disable the network.
  3. Navigate to a new page.

Expected:

  • The offline screen appears.
  • The sidebar remains visible.
  • No endless loader appears.
  • Retry is available.

Scenario 2: PWA opened while offline

  1. Install the Panorra PWA.
  2. Open it once while online.
  3. Close the application.
  4. Disable the network.
  5. Reopen the PWA.

Expected:

  • The cached offline screen loads.
  • The logo and illustration are available.
  • No broken-image placeholders appear.

Scenario 3: Retry while still offline

  1. Display the offline screen.
  2. Select Try again.

Expected:

  • The button enters a checking state.
  • The check times out safely.
  • The user remains on the offline screen.
  • A clear offline message remains visible.

Scenario 4: Connection returns

  1. Display the offline screen.
  2. Restore the network.

Expected:

  • Panorra verifies backend availability.
  • The original page is retried.
  • A back-online message may appear.
  • The application does not repeatedly reload.

Scenario 5: Captive portal or unreachable backend

  1. Connect to a network without usable internet.
  2. Open Panorra.

Expected:

  • navigator.onLine may be true.
  • The health check fails.
  • Panorra correctly shows the offline screen.

Scenario 6: Dark mode

  1. Enable dark mode.
  2. Open Panorra offline.

Expected:

  • Dark surfaces render correctly.
  • The illustration remains vibrant.
  • Text, buttons, and borders remain readable.
  • The primary color remains consistent with the brand.

16. Analytics Events

Recommended events:

Event Trigger
offline_screen_view Offline fallback becomes visible
offline_retry_select User selects Try again
offline_retry_success Connectivity is restored
offline_retry_fail Retry fails
offline_return_home User selects the return action
connection_restored Panorra confirms backend reachability

Recommended parameters:

source_route
retry_count
connection_check_duration_bucket
theme
pwa_installed

Do not send:

  • IP addresses
  • Precise coordinates
  • Raw error messages
  • Authentication tokens
  • Private page content
  • User-generated text

Analytics must respect the user’s analytics-consent preference.

17. Engineering Effort Rationale

Estimated relative effort

Solution Relative effort Ongoing maintenance
Offline fallback screen Low Low
Cached static application shell Low Low
Cached feed and place data Medium Medium
Offline mutations and synchronization High High
Downloadable 360° media High High
Full offline maps Very high Very high

Why the simple fallback is efficient

The selected solution avoids engineering effort in:

  • Database schema design for local storage
  • Data migration
  • Cache invalidation
  • Storage cleanup
  • Upload resumption
  • Conflict resolution
  • Retry queues
  • Media-download controls
  • Background-sync compatibility
  • Browser-specific offline defects
  • Offline security review
  • Complex QA matrices

The team can instead focus on Panorra’s core online experience:

  • Discovery
  • 360° viewing
  • Upload quality
  • Maps
  • Community features
  • Performance
  • Reliability

18. Conditions for Expanding Offline Support

Panorra should only invest in advanced offline functionality when product evidence supports it.

Possible triggers:

  • A meaningful percentage of sessions encounter poor connectivity
  • Users repeatedly request saved offline content
  • Travel users are a major segment
  • Offline failures materially reduce retention
  • Support tickets show clear demand
  • Downloadable 360° tours become a paid feature
  • Map access without connectivity becomes strategically important

Before expanding, measure:

  • offline_screen_view
  • Retry success rate
  • Offline abandonment rate
  • Routes most affected by connection loss
  • User regions with weak connectivity
  • Frequency of repeated offline sessions

19. Future Roadmap

If evidence justifies further work, use this sequence:

Phase 1 — Approved now

  • Offline fallback page
  • Retry
  • Return action
  • Automatic recovery
  • Light and dark themes

Phase 2 — Low-complexity improvement

  • Local post drafts
  • Last viewed page restoration
  • Small static help content

Phase 3 — Explicit user downloads

  • Download selected 360° photos
  • Storage usage display
  • Delete downloaded content
  • Wi-Fi-only download setting

Phase 4 — Lightweight offline actions

  • Save place
  • Like post
  • Follow creator
  • Join community

This phase requires idempotent APIs and visible pending states.

Phase 5 — Advanced offline experience

  • Cached place details
  • Downloaded map areas
  • Background synchronization
  • Conflict resolution
  • Cross-device reconciliation

This phase should be treated as a separate product initiative.

20. Definition of Done

The feature is complete when:

  • The offline screen is implemented in the Next.js PWA.
  • The production sidebar is used.
  • The illustration uses the Panorra logo gradient.
  • The screen works in light and dark modes.
  • Try again performs a real health check.
  • Automatic recovery works.
  • The fallback is available from the service-worker cache.
  • No large dynamic content is cached.
  • Accessibility checks pass.
  • Analytics events respect consent.
  • Product, design, engineering, and QA approve the behavior.

21. Final Product Statement

Panorra will handle loss of connectivity with a simple, branded, and actionable offline screen rather than a full offline-content system.

This decision:

  • Solves the immediate usability problem
  • Protects the product from broken loading states
  • Preserves Panorra’s visual identity
  • Minimizes storage and privacy risks
  • Avoids complex synchronization work
  • Reduces testing and maintenance costs
  • Prevents wasted engineering effort
  • Leaves room for evidence-driven expansion later

The guiding principle is:

Build the smallest reliable offline experience that solves the user’s problem today, and only add offline complexity when user behavior proves that it is necessary.

Panorra 360 Upload Flow Product Specification

1. Overview

This document defines the product specification and acceptance criteria for the Panorra 360 image upload flow.

The upload step supports three input methods:

  • Browse Files
  • Dropbox
  • Embed Link

The upload interface must help users add a valid 360 image, preview the result, and continue to the next creation step.

2. Product Goal

The upload flow should:

  • Make all upload methods easy to discover
  • Keep the three methods inside one consistent interface
  • Validate 360 image requirements before continuing
  • Show clear progress and error states
  • Allow users to preview the imported panorama
  • Support third-party embedded panorama sources
  • Prevent users from continuing until a valid source is ready

3. Main Layout

The desktop screen contains three primary regions:

  1. Primary navigation sidebar
  2. Upload control panel
  3. Main preview canvas

Recommended proportions

Region Recommended width
Primary navigation sidebar 72 to 88 px
Upload control panel 360 to 460 px
Main preview canvas Remaining width

The preview canvas should remain the dominant area after a panorama has been loaded.

4. Step Header

The upload step header appears at the top of the control panel.

Required content

  • Step label: Step 1: Add Image
  • Step progress: 1 Out of 3
  • Back button
  • Next button

Behavior

  • Back returns to the previous flow.
  • Next advances to the following creation step.
  • Next remains disabled until a valid image or embed source is ready.

Acceptance criteria

  • The current step is always visible.
  • Progress text accurately reflects the workflow.
  • The Next button uses disabled styling before validation succeeds.
  • The Next button becomes enabled after a valid source loads.
  • Back does not remove uploaded data unless the user confirms leaving.

5. Upload Method Tabs

The upload area includes three method tabs:

  1. Browse Files
  2. Dropbox
  3. Embed

Behavior

  • Only one upload method is active at a time.
  • Switching methods does not automatically delete a completed upload.
  • The active method uses a distinct visual state.
  • The relevant method panel appears directly below the tabs.

Acceptance criteria

  • All three methods remain visible.
  • Tabs are keyboard accessible.
  • Switching tabs does not trigger a full page reload.
  • The current method is announced to screen readers.
  • Unsaved input is preserved where practical.

6. Method 1: Browse Files

Purpose

Allows users to upload a 360 image from their local device.

Components

  • Drag-and-drop area
  • Browse Files button
  • Supported file message
  • Upload progress state
  • Uploaded file row
  • Remove file action
  • Next button

Accepted input

Recommended baseline:

  • JPG
  • JPEG
  • 2:1 aspect ratio
  • Maximum file size defined by backend constraints

Empty state text

Drag and drop your 360 image here or click to browse files.

Helper text

JPG/JPEG with a 2:1 aspect ratio is accepted.

Uploaded file row

The uploaded file row should include:

  • Thumbnail
  • File name
  • File size
  • Upload status
  • Remove action

Behavior

  • Users can drag a file into the drop zone.
  • Users can click Browse Files to open the native file picker.
  • Validation runs before upload begins.
  • The upload row replaces the empty drop zone after selection.
  • Removing the file returns the panel to the empty state.

Acceptance criteria

  • Unsupported formats are rejected with a clear message.
  • Incorrect aspect ratios are rejected or flagged.
  • Upload progress is visible.
  • Failed uploads provide a retry action.
  • The Next button becomes enabled only after successful upload and preview generation.
  • The preview canvas displays the uploaded panorama.
  • Removing the file disables Next.

7. Method 2: Dropbox

Purpose

Allows users to select a 360 image from Dropbox.

Components

  • Dropbox connection state
  • Connect Dropbox button
  • Dropbox file browser
  • Folder breadcrumb
  • File list
  • Single-select control
  • Next button

Connection state

Before connection:

  • Dropbox logo
  • Short explanation
  • Connect Dropbox button

Example text:

Connect to your Dropbox to select a 360 image.

File browser state

After connection, display:

  • Current folder path
  • File thumbnail
  • File name
  • File size
  • Selection control
  • Scrollable list when needed

Behavior

  • Selecting Connect Dropbox opens the authorization flow.
  • After authorization, the user returns to the upload panel.
  • Only supported image files appear or remain selectable.
  • Selecting a file loads it into the main preview.
  • Only one file can be selected at a time.

Acceptance criteria

  • The connection state is clear.
  • Authentication failures display a recovery action.
  • The selected file uses a visible active state.
  • Unsupported files cannot be selected.
  • The Next button becomes enabled after a valid file loads.
  • The preview updates when the selected Dropbox file changes.
  • Revoked access is handled without losing the rest of the editor state.

8. Method 3: Embed Link

Purpose

Allows users to import a panorama from a supported third-party platform.

Supported platforms

  • TourMkr
  • Villume
  • Google Street View

Components

  • Platform selector
  • Platform logo
  • URL input
  • Apply Link button
  • Validation message
  • Supported-platform information
  • Preview result

Platform selector behavior

The selector displays:

  • TourMkr
  • Villume
  • Google Street View

The selected platform determines:

  • Logo
  • Placeholder URL
  • URL validation rules
  • Import method

URL input examples

TourMkr

https://tourmkr.com/...

Villume

Use the valid Villume share or embed URL pattern.

Google Street View

Use the supported Google Maps or Street View share URL pattern.

Apply Link behavior

  • Disabled when the input is empty.
  • Enabled when the URL has a valid basic structure.
  • Triggers URL validation and import.
  • Displays loading feedback while resolving the source.
  • Loads the panorama into the preview after success.

Acceptance criteria

  • The user must select a platform before applying a link.
  • The URL must match the selected platform.
  • Invalid links produce platform-specific guidance.
  • Unsupported or private links display an error.
  • The Apply Link button cannot be triggered repeatedly during processing.
  • The Next button becomes enabled only after the embed preview loads.
  • Changing the platform clears incompatible validation errors.
  • The supported-platform note remains visible.

9. Embed Platform Selector

Default state

Recommended default:

TourMkr

Dropdown items

Each item should include:

  • Platform logo
  • Platform name

Acceptance criteria

  • The dropdown has a visible label: Select Platform.
  • Logos remain aligned and legible.
  • Keyboard users can open and select options.
  • The selected option is clearly shown.
  • The URL placeholder changes after selection.

10. Main Preview Canvas

The main preview canvas displays the loaded panorama.

Empty state

Before upload or import:

  • Dashed upload placeholder
  • Image upload icon
  • Instruction text
  • Supported format text

Loaded state

After successful upload:

  • Interactive 360 preview
  • Fit-to-screen control
  • Zoom controls where supported
  • Back and Next controls near the preview on large layouts where useful

Acceptance criteria

  • The empty state is centered.
  • The preview maintains the correct panorama projection.
  • Preview loading feedback appears during processing.
  • The preview displays independently from the upload method.
  • Changing source updates the preview.
  • The preview failure state provides Retry and Remove actions.

11. Filters and Animation Controls

The existing upload screen may include disabled controls for:

  • Filter
  • North Angle
  • Zoom
  • Animate Image

These controls should remain disabled until a valid panorama is loaded.

Acceptance criteria

  • Disabled controls use clear non-interactive styling.
  • After upload, controls become enabled only when supported.
  • Users cannot change filter or animation values before a source is ready.
  • The state remains consistent across upload methods.

12. Source Switching Rules

When no source has been completed

Users may switch methods freely.

When a valid source already exists

Recommended behavior:

  • Preserve the current source until the user confirms replacing it.
  • Show a confirmation dialog before destructive replacement.

Example:

Replace the current panorama? Your existing upload will be removed.

Acceptance criteria

  • Users do not lose a valid upload accidentally.
  • Replacement confirmation identifies the existing source.
  • Cancel keeps the current preview and method state.
  • Confirm clears the previous source and activates the new method.

13. Validation Rules

Local and Dropbox images

Validate:

  • File type
  • File size
  • Aspect ratio
  • Image readability
  • Minimum resolution
  • Corrupted file state

Embed links

Validate:

  • URL format
  • Platform match
  • Public accessibility
  • Embeddable resource availability
  • Panorama compatibility

Acceptance criteria

  • Validation messages appear near the affected field.
  • Messages explain how to fix the issue.
  • Validation does not rely on color alone.
  • Next remains disabled until all required checks pass.

14. Loading States

Browse Files

  • File validation
  • Upload progress
  • Image processing
  • Preview generation

Dropbox

  • Connecting
  • Loading folders
  • Loading files
  • Importing selected file
  • Preview generation

Embed

  • Validating URL
  • Resolving external resource
  • Loading panorama
  • Preview generation

Acceptance criteria

  • Each asynchronous action displays feedback.
  • Buttons prevent duplicate actions while loading.
  • Loading indicators identify the current task.
  • Users can cancel where technically supported.

15. Error States

Browse Files errors

  • Unsupported file type
  • File too large
  • Invalid aspect ratio
  • Corrupted image
  • Upload failed

Dropbox errors

  • Authorization failed
  • Permission revoked
  • File unavailable
  • Import failed
  • Network error

Embed errors

  • Invalid URL
  • Platform mismatch
  • Private source
  • Unsupported source
  • Source unavailable
  • Preview could not be generated

Example messages

This image does not use the required 2:1 panorama ratio.

This link does not appear to be a valid TourMkr URL.

We could not access this Dropbox file. Check its permissions and try again.

16. Accessibility Requirements

  • Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirements.
  • Use visible labels for all inputs.
  • Provide clear focus states.
  • Support keyboard navigation across tabs, buttons, dropdowns, and file rows.
  • Announce upload progress and errors to screen readers.
  • Provide accessible names for icon-only actions.
  • Ensure the drop zone can be activated without drag-and-drop.
  • Maintain minimum touch target sizes on mobile.

17. Responsive Behavior

Desktop

  • Fixed navigation sidebar
  • Fixed-width upload panel
  • Large preview canvas

Tablet

  • Sidebar may collapse to icons
  • Upload panel may become narrower
  • Preview remains beside the panel where space permits

Mobile

Recommended behavior:

  • Upload panel becomes full width
  • Preview appears below or above the method controls
  • Upload tabs remain horizontally scrollable if needed
  • Next action remains sticky
  • Dropbox file rows use full-width layout
  • Embed form stacks vertically

Acceptance criteria

  • No horizontal overflow occurs.
  • The active upload method remains clear.
  • Buttons remain reachable.
  • The preview stays usable at supported breakpoints.

18. Analytics Events

Recommended events:

Event Trigger
upload_step_viewed User opens Step 1
upload_method_selected User changes upload method
local_file_selected User selects a local file
local_upload_completed Local upload succeeds
local_upload_failed Local upload fails
dropbox_connect_started User starts Dropbox connection
dropbox_connected Connection succeeds
dropbox_file_selected User selects a Dropbox file
dropbox_import_completed Dropbox import succeeds
embed_platform_selected User selects an embed platform
embed_link_submitted User applies an embed link
embed_import_completed Embed import succeeds
embed_import_failed Embed import fails
upload_source_replaced User replaces the current source
upload_step_completed User selects Next

Recommended properties

  • upload method
  • platform
  • file type
  • file size
  • validation result
  • processing duration
  • error code
  • viewport size

19. Suggested Data Model

Upload source

{
  "method": "embed",
  "status": "ready",
  "sourceId": "source_001",
  "previewUrl": "/preview/source_001",
  "originalUrl": "https://tourmkr.com/example",
  "platform": "tourmkr"
}

Local file

{
  "id": "file_001",
  "name": "office_lobby_360.jpg",
  "sizeBytes": 2516582,
  "mimeType": "image/jpeg",
  "width": 6000,
  "height": 3000,
  "aspectRatio": "2:1",
  "uploadStatus": "complete"
}

Dropbox file

{
  "id": "dbx_001",
  "name": "meeting_room_360.jpg",
  "sizeBytes": 3250585,
  "thumbnailUrl": "/dropbox/thumb/dbx_001",
  "path": "/360 Images/meeting_room_360.jpg",
  "selected": true
}

Embed platform

{
  "id": "tourmkr",
  "name": "TourMkr",
  "logoUrl": "/assets/platforms/tourmkr.svg",
  "urlPattern": "^https://(www\\.)?tourmkr\\.com/"
}

Upload state

{
  "activeMethod": "browse",
  "source": null,
  "isProcessing": false,
  "canContinue": false,
  "error": null
}

20. Acceptance Criteria Summary

The upload flow is complete when:

  • Browse Files, Dropbox, and Embed appear as distinct upload methods.
  • Only one method is active at a time.
  • Local upload supports drag-and-drop and file browsing.
  • Dropbox supports connection, file browsing, and single selection.
  • Embed supports TourMkr, Villume, and Google Street View.
  • Embed requires platform selection, URL entry, and Apply Link.
  • Next remains disabled until a valid panorama loads.
  • The preview updates for all three methods.
  • Source replacement is protected by confirmation.
  • Validation, loading, empty, and error states are implemented.
  • The flow works across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
  • Accessibility and analytics requirements are met.

21. Definition of Done

The feature is ready for release when:

  • Product approves the three upload methods.
  • Design approves the upload tabs, forms, and preview states.
  • Engineering completes local, Dropbox, and embed integrations.
  • QA validates supported and unsupported files.
  • QA validates each embed platform.
  • Preview rendering works for every valid source type.
  • Next state logic is reliable.
  • Accessibility checks pass.
  • Analytics events are verified.
  • Error recovery paths are tested.

Panorra Brand Identity Guide

Web development reference for Panorra, a 360° social media platform for immersive photos, videos, places, and communities.

1. Brand Overview

Brand name: Panorra
Category: 360° social media and location discovery platform
Core experience: Explore, publish, and share immersive 360° photos and videos connected to real-world places.

Brand idea

Panorra helps people experience places beyond flat images.

The brand should feel:

  • Immersive
  • Modern
  • Explorative
  • Social
  • Creative
  • Trustworthy
  • Premium

Brand positioning

Explore places from every angle.

Supporting tagline options

  • See more. Feel present.
  • Discover the world in 360°.
  • Share places beyond the frame.
  • Every place has another angle.

2. Primary Brand Direction

Panorra uses a soft blue-violet as its main product color.

This direction is softer than Electric Indigo, while still feeling modern, digital, immersive, and recognizable.

Primary color

Token Value
Name Panorra Blue Violet
Hex #6F64E6
