30. Theme Initialization

Apply the user’s saved theme before the interface is rendered to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

<script>
  (() => {
    const savedTheme = localStorage.getItem("panorra-theme");
    const systemPrefersDark = window.matchMedia(
      "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
    ).matches;

    const theme =
      savedTheme === "light" || savedTheme === "dark"
        ? savedTheme
        : systemPrefersDark
          ? "dark"
          : "light";

    document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme;
  })();
</script>

Recommended theme values

  • light
  • dark
  • system

When the saved value is system, follow the operating system preference.

31. JavaScript Theme Controller

const themeMedia = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");

function resolveTheme(preference) {
  if (preference === "system") {
    return themeMedia.matches ? "dark" : "light";
  }

  return preference;
}

function applyTheme(preference) {
  const resolvedTheme = resolveTheme(preference);

  document.documentElement.dataset.theme = resolvedTheme;
  document.documentElement.dataset.themePreference = preference;
  localStorage.setItem("panorra-theme", preference);
}

themeMedia.addEventListener("change", () => {
  const preference =
    localStorage.getItem("panorra-theme") || "system";

  if (preference === "system") {
    applyTheme("system");
  }
});

        : "system";
    });

  const [systemTheme, setSystemTheme] =
    useState<ResolvedTheme>(() => getSystemTheme());

  useEffect(() => {
    const media = window.matchMedia(
      "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
    );

    const handleChange = () => {
      setSystemTheme(media.matches ? "dark" : "light");
    };

    media.addEventListener("change", handleChange);

    return () => {
      media.removeEventListener("change", handleChange);
    };
  }, []);

  const resolvedTheme: ResolvedTheme =
    preference === "system" ? systemTheme : preference;

  useEffect(() => {
    document.documentElement.dataset.theme = resolvedTheme;
    document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = resolvedTheme;
    localStorage.setItem("panorra-theme", preference);
  }, [preference, resolvedTheme]);

  const value = useMemo(
    () => ({
      preference,
      resolvedTheme,
      setPreference: setPreferenceState,
    }),
    [preference, resolvedTheme]
  );

  return (
    <ThemeContext.Provider value={value}>
      {children}
    </ThemeContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useTheme() {
  const context = useContext(ThemeContext);

  if (!context) {
    throw new Error(
      "useTheme must be used inside ThemeProvider"
    );
  }

  return context;
}

  • Verify all text and interactive states against WCAG AA contrast requirements.
  • Avoid pure white on pure black for large reading surfaces.
  • Use #F8FAFC rather than #FFFFFF for most body text.

  • Do not reduce border visibility too far.
  • Do not use blue-violet text for long paragraphs.

  • Test media overlays over both bright and dark imagery.
  • Test at 200% browser zoom.
  • Test the 360° viewer with reduced motion enabled.

🔀 Integrate Prev/Next Fullscreen — From Search (Post / Hashtag Post)

Wire prev/next navigation in the fullscreen viewer when entered from Search results — the Search Post tab and Hashtag post results — so the user can move through those results without leaving fullscreen.

Based on pages-new (pages-new/fullscreen/* + Search Discover results — see #3107, Search Post #3118 / Hashtag #3120). Sibling contexts: Profile, Timeline.

Scope

  • When opening /fullscreen/:slug from Search results (Post tab or a Hashtag's posts), carry the ordered result list + current index + the active query/hashtag so the viewer can go prev/next (arrows/swipe) and fetch the next results page when it runs out (continue the search pagination). Update the URL/slug on navigation. Signal-driven; no BehaviorSubject, no any.

🧪 Test scenario (for QA)

  1. Enter (Post) — open a search-result post in fullscreen → prev/next available.
  2. Enter (Hashtag) — open a post from a hashtag's results → prev/next traverses that hashtag's posts.
  3. Navigate — next/prev moves through the search results in order; slug/URL updates; the query/hashtag context is preserved.
  4. Boundaries — first has no prev; last loads the next results page (or stops at the end).
  5. Back / types — leaving fullscreen returns to the search results at the right position; panorama/multiple/video/embed render correctly; no console errors.

Acceptance: prev/next traverses the search (post + hashtag) results (with pagination) from fullscreen; query context + slug/URL + boundaries + back-position handled; no any.
